headline: UN experts say US strikes in Iran may be war crimes
summary: Three UN experts say there are reasonable grounds to believe the US committed war crimes in two February strikes in Iran. One hit a primary school in Minab, killing at least 156 people, 120 of them children, local officials say. The other hit a sports complex in Lamerd. The US says it is investigating Minab and denies striking Lamerd.
cover_answer: Three UN experts, for now. They point at the US, twice.
table_question: If you break a rule by accident, should the punishment be smaller?

5-7.script: In a war far away, a missile hit a school in Iran and many children died. Experts who work for the United Nations say the American military fired it and broke the rules of war. Wars have rules, the way a playground does, and someone checks whether they were followed. You are safe here, and the grown-ups are working out what happened.
5-7.why: If it comes up, the idea that even wars have rules gives a small child something to hold.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: Wars have rules. One is that you check a target is military before you fire. Three UN experts say the US did not check before two strikes in Iran. The US denies one and is investigating the other. Like a referee reviewing a play: this is the review, not the ruling.
8-12.why: Rule, break, review is a chain they already know from sports.

13-17.script: Who judges a war crime? Three UN experts say there are reasonable grounds to believe the US committed two in Iran, one of them a strike on a school. The US never answered their questions. Who checks the checkers?
13-17.why: Teens can weigh an accusation without deciding guilt.

5-7.q: Did our country do something bad?
5-7.a: Some experts say the US broke the rules of war. The US says it is still checking what happened. The grown-ups are sorting it out.

8-12.q: Are there rules in a war?
8-12.a: Yes. One is that you check a target is military before you hit it. The UN experts say the US didn't.

8-12.q: What happens to the US now?
8-12.a: Nothing automatic. The report goes to the UN Human Rights Council. The US has not commented on it.

13-17.a: For now, these three experts. Their words are 'reasonable grounds to believe,' not a verdict.

13-17.q: Didn't Trump say it was a mistake?
13-17.a: In June he said 'nobody did that on purpose.' The experts say the school was hit twice and was the intended target.
